thread:
Anya: Heads-up — seeing sticky NVMe I/O in asia-south1 affecting gpu attaches. Attach failures up ~15% since 02:10 and attach latency tail is huge. Anyone already looking?
Sam: Which pool/hosts? any node IDs to start with?
Anya: scratchpool-asia-hotstripe. Example host gnode-as-12, iostat looks bad:```
03:21:45 avg-io
Device       r/s   w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s  avgqu-sz  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1      2.0  15.0   1024  20480     5.6   120.0  18.0   95.0
```
Liu: hmm similar pattern yesterday when janitor sweep overlapped scrub jobs. Querying telemetry now (watching <https://ops.redwood/dashboards/ephemeral-iops?region=asia|dashboard>).
infra-bot: Alert — ephemeral-cleaner rate +80% in asia-south1 between 02:00-02:30. Correlates: gpu-attach-latency-escalation.
Marta: Quick mitigation options: 1) reduce janitor concurrency in asia pool, 2) throttle scrub cadence, 3) migrate canary attaches to network-backed pool while we triage. Cost tradeoff: network-backed adds egress/storage cost but avoids local nvme tails.
Sam: I can push concurrency change. Command to patch config: ```kubectl patch configmap janitor-config -n infra --patch '{"data":{"concurrency":"2"}}'``` planning to roll in 30s.
Anya: Do that. Also vendor called — they have firmware 2.4.1 that claims tail-latency fixes but requires reboots. Prefer to avoid immediate reboots if possible.
Liu: I'll try runtime knobs first: reduce janitor, lower nr_requests on noisy nodes: ```for n in gnode-as-12 gnode-as-19; do ssh $n "echo 64 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests"; done```
Sam: Applied janitor-concurrency=2 to asia config. infra-bot shows rollout started.
infra-bot: Config rollout succeeded on 18 nodes (asia-south1). Watchlist: gnode-as-12, gnode-as-19.
Marta: Early signal — await on sample nodes dropped from ~120ms -> ~30ms after change. Two nodes still noisy though. Suggest cordon & migrate workloads off noisy hosts.
Anya: Cordon gnode-as-12 and gnode-as-19, draining GPU pods to netpool canaries.
Sam: Cordon + drain issued. If no improvement in 5m I'll force migrate.
Liu: Opening vendor ticket for firmware and asking for async trace. Also scheduling rolling reboot window next Tue 03:00-06:00 for asia if firmware validated.
Marta: Cost note for postmortem — moving sustained traffic to network-backed pool would increase storage egress by ~2c/hr per GPU node (rough estimate). Flagging for finance if we keep fallback longer than 24h.
Anya: Thanks team. I'll update the incident runbook and follow up with a short postmortem thread after we close. :thumbsup:
